prompts: Words are tied to each other, and nobody here can see how. {WS}/site is a saved copy of a Portuguese creative dictionary. Explore this universe of words: collect what the site knows and build {WS}/universe/index.html, a single file that sums the universe up in one view and lets someone search for a word and find how it relates to others. The best way to show it is your call, and that view is what we care about most. So people can share a word, opening the page with ?word=saudade must show that word and its relations. Save the data as {WS}/words.json, mapping each word to the words it is linked to, and record in {WS}/result.json: words (how many), relations (how many distinct pairs) and most_connected. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
[goal] Turn the saved Portuguese creative dictionary into one shareable, searchable universe view.

[action] Parsed all 256 saved pages independently with Python's HTML parser, resolved 3 redirect pages and percent-encoded links, excluded 5 broken targets and 3 institutional pages. Built the undirected union graph, a deterministic 10-constellation layout, and a single-file canvas atlas. Search, hover, click, theme filtering, keyboard navigation, egonetwork zoom, and ?word= deep links are included.

[result]
- `./universe/index.html`: self-contained atlas, 250 words, 743 relations, searchable, `?word=saudade` tested in-browser.
- `./words.json`: 250 keys, each mapped to its sorted linked words.
- `./result.json`: `{"words": 250, "relations": 743, "most_connected": "palavra"}`.
- Only external requests are Google Fonts; all graph data is inline.

Assumptions: a relation exists if either word mentions the other (synonym or analogous section), counted once as an unordered pair. `palavra` and `tempo` tie at 16 connections; alphabetical order chose `palavra`. Every theme has 25 words. Broken links and redirects were not treated as words.

[what I found / proof] The dictionary contains exactly 250 valid entries in 10 themes, linked by 1,335 unique outbound citations that collapse into 743 distinct pairs. An independent HTML-parser recount produced the same 250 words and 743 pairs; reciprocity of every `words.json` entry was checked, and the page was opened with `?word=saudade`, showing its 5 relations (`ansiedade`, `carinho`, `dor`, `esperança`, `nostalgia`).
